svg.title: Breadboard assembly and labeled wiring for the flex-sensor glove
svg.desc: Top: a one-sensor divider with numbered breadboard rows and columns. Uno 5V feeds the positive rail and row 5; the sensor connects e5 to e10. A0 reads a10. A 10 kilohm resistor connects c10 to c15, and a15 connects to ground. Bottom: named-pin wiring for each radio, local bypass capacitors and a receiver servo with a separate supply. Conceptual Uno pin breakouts are labeled by name, not physical header position.
svg.text: Flex-sensor glove · breadboard assembly and pin-by-pin wiring
Original reference drawing · power off while wiring · Uno pins shown as labeled breakouts, not header positions
Connected strips: a–e on one row; f–j on the same row are a separate strip. The center gap is not connected.
Red: +5 V · black: GND · green: A0 signal
Crossings without dots do not join.
Example uses rows 5, 10 and 15. Verify continuity: rail breaks and printed coordinates vary by breadboard.
Do not join the 5 V rail to a radio VCC pin. The radio uses the Uno 3.3V pin separately.
2 / Wireless option · repeat on BOTH Unos
Use female jumpers or a labeled breakout; match printed pin names.
C1 = 100 nF ceramic; C2 = 10 µF (+ to VCC, − to GND).
Place both next to the radio. IRQ is not connected.
This is a named-pin breakout, NOT the 2×4 header pin order.
Do not push a bare 2×4 radio header into common 5-hole strips.
3.3 V supply; direct Uno signals require Nordic VDD conditions.
Power return goes directly to the external supply.
Never power the servo through the Uno or 5 V rail.
Do not route motor current through the breadboard.
Supply − joins receiver GND; supply + stays separate.
Check polarity and unloaded servo travel first.
Reference illustration, not a bench-tested assembly. Check actual module labels, rail continuity and electrical limits before power-up.
Original SVG · MIT · See hardware/README.md and BUILD_GUIDE.md for the connection table, primary sources and staged checks.
